title: Rhythm Red and the league of hoofers
summary: Green praises John Rhythm Red Shivers as having brought hoofers to box office, and says the league of tap dancers originally numbered thirteen.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Let's go on now, Chuck, to some of the other real powerhouses of tap dancing during that era, people like Rhythm Red, what he was doing.

Oh, John. Yeah, John Rhythm Red Shivers. Yeah. Well, see he was -- see, he was known as Debut, you know, Debut John. That's what I used to call him. And when he was -- we was kind of raised up -- we grew up together. We come up as youngsters (unintelligible) -- around the fraternity uptown, you know.
And Rhythm Red was really the causing of the hoofers actually getting into their -- to today's popularity, you see, and becoming box office finally, you see.

Well, they are a team, a league of tap dancers, you see. Originally there were 13, see. And there was some teachers there. Quite a few of them are teachers, you see. And they got a chance to work at the Burt Wheeler Theater here, and the Dixie Hotel.
